description: Load test client metrics + SLO compliance

panels.description: Normal: < 500ms (green). Watch for: crossing 500ms (yellow) or 1s (red) sustained. Check next: E2E Move Latency panel for percentile trend over time.
panels.title: E2E p95

panels.description: Normal: < 200ms (green). Watch for: crossing 200ms (yellow) or 500ms (red) sustained. Check next: WS Delivery Latency panel for percentile breakdown.
panels.title: WS Delivery p95

panels.description: Normal: < 50ms (green). Watch for: crossing 50ms (yellow) or 100ms (red) sustained. Check next: System Health DB Pool panels for saturation evidence.
panels.title: DB Txn p95

panels.description: Normal: < 1% (green). Watch for: crossing 1% (yellow) or 5% (red) sustained. Check next: Error Breakdown panel for error type categorization.
panels.title: HTTP Error Rate

panels.description: Normal: matches configured concurrency. Watch for: stuck at 0 (no games starting) or exceeding target (games not completing). Check next: Completion Rate and Game Completion panels.
panels.title: Active Games

panels.description: Normal: proportional to active games. Watch for: sudden drops (server overload) or flat at zero (test harness stuck). Check next: E2E Move Latency to see if slowdown explains throughput drop.
panels.title: Throughput

panels.description: Normal: > 95% (green). Watch for: dropping below 80% (yellow) means too many timeouts or fatals. Check next: Error Breakdown for error types causing failures.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="perftest", span_name=~"perftest[.]game[.]run", status_code!="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[1m])) or vector(0)) / (sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="perftest", span_name=~"perftest[.]game[.]run"}[1m])) or vector(1))

panels.title: Completion Rate

panels.description: Normal: zero or near-zero. Watch for: any sustained error rate or new error types appearing. Check next: System Health dashboard for server-side error details.
panels.title: Error Breakdown

panels.description: Normal: dense band below 500ms. Watch for: color spreading into higher buckets (latency distribution widening under load). Check next: Percentile Bands below for exact P50/P95/P99 values.
panels.title: E2E Latency Heatmap

panels.description: Normal: tight bands with P95 < 500ms. Watch for: bands widening (latency variance increasing) or P99 diverging from P95 (tail latency problem). Check next: Latency Attribution to identify which server boundary causes the spread.
panels.title: E2E Latency Percentile Bands

panels.description: Normal: DB + game logic + WS sum to roughly HTTP total; event handler runs independently after response. Watch for: one boundary dominating (e.g. DB > 70% of HTTP) or event handler exceeding HTTP total. Check next: Database dashboard if DB dominates, WebSocket dashboard if WS dominates.
panels.title: Latency Attribution (p95)

panels.description: Normal: P95 < 500ms, P99 < 1s. Watch for: P95 crossing the threshold line (SLO breach). Check next: REST Latency by Action to identify which move type is slowest.
panels.title: E2E Move Latency (P50/P95/P99)

panels.description: Normal: P95 < 200ms. Watch for: P95 crossing the threshold line (WS delivery SLO breach). Check next: WebSocket dashboard for connection and broadcast details.
panels.title: WS Delivery Latency (P50/P95/P99)

panels.description: Normal: all actions < 200ms at P95. Watch for: single action diverging (e.g. attack P95 spiking while others stay flat). Check next: Database dashboard for query-level latency.
panels.title: Move Latency by Action (P50/P95/P99)

panels.description: Normal: low, proportional to concurrency. Watch for: conflicts/s exceeding moves/s (more retries than successes, contention too high). Check next: E2E Latency vs Concurrency to correlate conflict rate with load.
panels.title: Conflicts/sec

panels.description: Normal: latency stays flat as concurrency increases. Watch for: inflection point where latency climbs sharply with concurrency (saturation). Check next: Server Latency vs Concurrency to see if server-side shows the same knee.
panels.title: E2E Latency vs Concurrency

panels.description: Normal: HTTP P95 < 100ms regardless of concurrency. Watch for: server latency rising before client E2E does (server is the bottleneck). Check next: Latency Attribution in Orient to identify which server boundary dominates.
panels.title: Server Latency vs Concurrency

panels.description: Normal: effective approximates active. Watch for: growing gap means games are getting stuck (stalled/zombie). Check next: Health Decomposition panel for per-state waterfall.
panels.title: Effective Concurrency

panels.description: Normal: healthy dominates the stack, others near zero. Watch for: slow/stalled/zombie layers growing (games not making progress). Check next: Effective Concurrency panel for the gap metric, System Health for DB pool saturation.
panels.title: Health Decomposition

panels.description: Normal: deploy and attack phases are longest. Watch for: single phase P95 spiking while others stay flat. Check next: Move Latency by Action for per-action latency comparison.
panels.title: Phase Duration by Phase

panels.description: Normal: zero or near-zero. Watch for: any sustained error rate, especially new error types appearing. Check next: Game Completion panel to see if errors cause game failures.
panels.title: Error Rate by Type

panels.description: Normal: consistent across the test run. Watch for: game duration growing over time (server slowing down under sustained load). Check next: Moves per Game to check if duration increase is from more moves or slower moves.
panels.title: Game Duration (P50/P95)

panels.description: Normal: stable distribution determined by game logic, not server performance. Watch for: sudden changes in move count (game logic bug or strategy change). Check next: Game Duration to correlate move count with total time.
panels.title: Moves per Game (P50/P95)

panels.description: Normal: completed grows steadily, others stay flat. Watch for: timed-out or fatal counts climbing (server cannot finish games in time). Check next: Error Rate by Type for error categorization.
panels.title: Game Completion

title: Perf Test
